title: Closing game running in editor doesn't trigger NotificationWMCloseRequest
body:
### Tested versions


- Reproducible in v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e]
- Reproducible in v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439]


### System information

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200.8037) - Godot_v4.6.1-stable_win64

### Issue description

When closing the game while running it via the embedded window in the editor, the NotificationWMCloseRequest is not sent. (When running the game outside the editor, the notification is sent normally.)

This issue was already reported in this [ticket](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101863). The ticket was closed as solved, and the code was merged into the main branch in January ahead of the 4.6 release.

### Steps to reproduce

In the _ready function of a script attached to the root node (or any node), add 
`get_tree().set_auto_accept_quit(false)`

Then implement a function to catch the notification and perform any other necessary action before calling the quit method
```
func _notification(what):
	if what == NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST:
		save_data()
		print("saving player data...")
		get_tree().quit() # default behavior
```

See MRP package. It's a minimal project with a simple scene and control nodes, with a button to increase a counter. Upon exiting, the counter is saved to a file in the user space and loaded when the game opens.

When running the game in its own window, you can see from the output window the game file being loaded and then saved when closing. This doesn't happen when running the game in the embedded editor window.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[test-wm-close-request.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26256124/test-wm-close-request.zip)
